core\utils\motion\bezier.ts

Cubic-bezier easing evaluator — the CSS cubic-bezier(x1,y1,x2,y2)
Sourcesrc/core\utils\motion\bezier.ts
UX surfaceShared primitives every surface builds on — no direct UI.

Members

slope

The curve's derivative dB/ds for one axis — 3(1−s)²·a1 + 6(1−s)s·(a2−a1) + 3s²·(1−a2).

  • @param s Curve parameter 0..1.
  • @param a1 First control point ordinate.
  • @param a2 Second control point ordinate.
  • @returns The axis slope at s.

cubicBezier

Builds a cubic-bezier(x1,y1,x2,y2) easing function. The endpoints are pinned to (0,0) and (1,1) like the CSS function — callers keep control points inside the unit square; out-of-range x clamps to the endpoints.

  • @param x1 First control point x (0..1).
  • @param y1 First control point y.
  • @param x2 Second control point x (0..1).
  • @param y2 Second control point y.
  • @returns The easing map x ∈ [0,1] → y.

ease

Solves x(s) = x for s — Newton-Raphson seeded with x itself, then bisection when the tangent flattens below NEWTON_MIN_SLOPE (a near-zero slope makes Newton's step diverge; the curve is still monotone-in-x for sane control points so bisection always lands).

  • @param x Progress input 0..1.
  • @returns The y ordinate of the curve point whose x is x.
